classification.difficultyReason: Find a percentage volume, then use that result in a unit-price calculation.

content.prompt: The label on a 750 mL bottle of soft drink states that it contains 5% pure lemon juice.

children.label: a
children.prompt: How many millilitres of pure lemon juice does it contain?

answer.worked: $$\begin{align*}\text{Volume of lemon juice}&=\frac{5}{100}\times750\text{ mL}\\\text{Volume of lemon juice}&=37.5\text{ mL}\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: If pure lemon juice costs 50 cents per 100 mL, what is the value of the lemon juice in the bottle? Give your answer to the nearest cent.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\text{Cost of 1 mL}&=\frac{50}{100}\text{ cents}\\\text{Cost of 1 mL}&=0.5\text{ cents}\\\text{Cost of 37.5 mL}&=37.5\times0.5\text{ cents}\\\text{Cost of 37.5 mL}&=18.75\text{ cents}\end{align*}$$

The value is $19$ cents to the nearest cent.
